name: canvas-agent
description: The canvas's tools for kou agents on a canvas: see the board, create and wire nodes, send them work and read what they answer. Only agents on a canvas have it. Generated from kou-canvas's tools: go generate ./cmd/internal/canvascli.

tools.name: CanvasView
tools.description: Show the canvas you are on: every node (its ID, kind, title, status, place and size, ports, worktree), every connection between them, and free places beside your node. Look before you create, connect or remove anything: the canvas changes while you work. A busy kou agent that has shown nothing for 10 minutes or more is marked quiet: it waits on a long command, or it is stuck — its transcript tells. To message a node you know the title of, CanvasSend needs no look first.

detail.description: full adds the connections' templates and the notes' texts.

tools.name: CanvasSpawn
tools.description: Create a node on the canvas — a kou agent (the default), a terminal running a command or another coding agent, a note — beside your node unless you say where, and give it its first prompt. A kou agent is an agent like you with a session of its own, which the canvas talks to directly: make coders, reviewers and researchers kou agents, and give each one that writes code a worktree of its own. An agent you spawn (a kou agent, claude-code, codex, opencode) is wired to you: its output to your input, so what it answers comes back to you as a message; connect wires it otherwise, connect {} not at all. It answers the node's ID and place.

preset.description: What the node runs: agent (the default: a kou agent like you), shell, command (runs command), note, claude-code, codex, opencode, or a plugin's preset as plugin/preset.

title.description: Its title, which the other nodes see: short and telling.

command.description: For a command node: the command line it runs.

cwd.description: The directory it works in, relative to the workspace or absolute: where a terminal starts; for a kou agent without a worktree, the folder its tools and shell work in (its session stays this workspace's). A worktree goes before it.

worktree.description: Work in a git worktree of its own, made when missing: its name, its branch kou/<name>. One writer per worktree. A kou agent's worktree is named after its session, whatever the name.

base.description: The branch or commit a new worktree starts from; HEAD by default.

include.description: Paths of the workspace git does not carry (vendor/, a tool's folder, fonts) to copy into its worktree, which gets the submodules of the user's checkout by itself.

link.description: Such paths to link into its worktree instead of copying: shared with the user's checkout, for big things nobody writes.

prompt.description: Its first prompt, sent once it runs; for a note, its text.

config.description: More of its configuration, as its preset defines it: for a kou agent model, effort (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), instructions (its role), output, and reply (auto: what it answers at a turn's end goes back to the node that sent it a message; off: it answers nodes with CanvasSend only — a foreman's default); permission_mode for claude-code.

access.description: What its program may do on the canvas: talk by default for what an agent makes; build lets it make nodes too.

near.description: The node to place it beside: yours by default.

side.description: Which side of near: the first free one by default.

x.description: Where it goes, instead of beside near: its left edge.

w.description: Its width; its preset's by default.

h.description: Its height; its preset's by default.

connect.description: Wire it at once: from's output to its input, its output to to's input. A node is its ID or self, with :port when not out or in. Left out, an agent is wired to answer you, as {"to":"self"}, and nothing else is wired; {} wires nothing.

tools.name: CanvasRemove
tools.description: Remove a node from the canvas: one you made, or any with admin access. Its program ends — a kou agent's run is stopped, and its session deleted; its worktree stays, with its work.

keep_session.description: Only when the user asks to keep it: keeps a kou agent's session, which then shows in the user's session list as a session of its own. By default it is deleted with the node.

keep_worktree.description: Worktrees are always kept: only the user removes them.

tools.name: CanvasConnect
tools.description: Connect a node's output to another's input: what the first puts out — a command's output, an agent's answer at the end of its turn — goes to the second as a message.

from.description: The output: a node's ID or self, with :port when not out.

to.description: The input: a node's ID or self, with :port when not in.

template.description: What the message says: {{text}}, {{title}}, {{data.<path>}}, {{from.title}}, {{from.id}}; the output's text by default.

mode.description: approve holds each message until the user lets it go; a connection that closes a loop of agents starts so.

deliver.description: By default a kou agent gets each message at once — at work, it reads it between its tool calls — and a terminal once it is idle. queue makes a kou agent wait until its turn ends too; now types into a busy terminal.

tools.name: CanvasDisconnect
tools.description: Remove a connection: by its ID, or by the output and input it joins.

from.description: Or the output it leaves: node or node:port.

to.description: And the input it reaches: node or node:port.

tools.name: CanvasMove
tools.description: Move or resize a node, to keep the canvas tidy.

tools.name: CanvasSend
tools.description: Message a node — a prompt for an agent, a command for a shell — named by its ID or its title: one call, no need to look it up first. With wait, the call waits for the node's answer and returns it: an agent's answer at the end of its turn, a shell's command output. Without wait, an agent's answer comes to you later as a prompt that starts with [canvas] reply from — unless it is a foreman, or its config's reply is off: those answer with CanvasSend. A kou agent reads the text at once, between its tool calls; a terminal is given it once idle, and Enter is pressed after it; keys are pressed as tmux send-keys names them. With replace, the text takes the place of your last prompt to a kou agent — one its model refused, say — instead of coming after it: no need to remove the agent and start over.

node.description: The node: its ID (n_…) or its title.

text.description: The message: the prompt, or what to type.

wait.description: Wait for the node's answer to this message, and return it. A node that waits for your answer cannot be waited for in turn.

timeout_s.description: With wait: how long to wait at most, in seconds; 600 by default. An answer that comes later comes to you as a reply.

submit.description: Press Enter after the text: true by default.

keys.description: Keys to press after the text, as tmux names them: Enter, Tab, Escape, BSpace, Up, Down, Left, Right, Home, End, C-c, M-x, F1…

when.description: By default a kou agent reads it at once (between its tool calls) and a terminal once it is idle. idle makes a kou agent wait until its turn ends; now types into a busy terminal, and starts an idle kou agent even when its queue is paused.

replace.description: For a kou agent: the text replaces your last prompt to it, as an edited prompt does. Its session goes back to before that prompt — the agent forgets the prompt and all its run did of it, files aside — and runs this text from there. Only once its run is over, and only while no other prompt came after yours.

tools.name: CanvasRead
tools.description: Read a node: a terminal's latest lines or screen, the latest output of a node (a command's output, an agent's answer). With wait, wait first — until it is idle, gives its next output, or ends — instead of polling. To ask a node something and have its answer, CanvasSend with wait does it in one call.

node.description: The node: its ID (n_…), its title, or self.

what.description: tail (the default): a terminal's latest lines; screen: what it shows; output or answer: its latest output.

lines.description: How many lines of tail: 80 by default.

wait.description: Wait until the node is idle, gives its next output (or its run ends without one: refused, stopped, failed), or ends, then read.

after.description: With wait output: the count of outputs CanvasSend answered, so that an output given meanwhile counts.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait at most, in seconds: 600 by default.

tools.name: CanvasTranscript
tools.description: Read a node's raw transcript: its prompts, answers, reasoning, tool calls with their outcomes, notices, and what the canvas told it (kind peer). tail=N gives the last N entries, wherever you stopped; after=last reads on from where you last stopped reading the node, a cursor of yours for each filter of kinds and tools. An answer holds about 30 KB: when it says more, read on with after set to its next — what did not fit is not lost. Filter by kinds, tools and time; ask for notes or summaries when you look into a stall.

node.description: The node whose raw transcript to read: its ID, title, or self.

tail.description: The last N entries that match, 500 at most: what the node did lately. It moves no cursor, and does not go with after.

after.description: Read on after a cursor: the next of an answer, or last for where you stopped reading the node with the same kinds and tools. Neither after nor tail: from the session's start.

limit.description: Maximum entries: 50 by default, 500 at most; fewer when they would not fit the answer.

kinds.description: Only these entry kinds: peer is a message of the canvas, from another node.

tools.description: Only tool entries with these names.

since.description: Only entries at or after this RFC3339 time. A read with since or until moves no cursor.

until.description: Only entries at or before this RFC3339 time.

message_limit.description: Maximum bytes of message, reasoning and detail fields: 8 KiB by default, less for an entry too big for the answer.

output_limit.description: Maximum bytes of tool output, stderr and error fields: 4 KiB by default, less for an entry too big for the answer. An output the harness kept whole in a file names it.

include.description: Include the durable notes or recent summaries beside the entries.

format.description: text (the default): an entry a line or a block, at local times; json: the entries as the server gives them, with their IDs and cursors.

tools.name: CanvasSearch
tools.description: Search a node's persisted raw transcript with a case-insensitive regular expression, showing matching lines with context. Use nodes=children to search all nodes you look after; this is for locating evidence, while CanvasTranscript reads the structured incremental feed.

node.description: The node to search: its ID, title, or self; with nodes=children it is the parent context.

nodes.description: Search all of your children instead of only node.

q.description: A case-insensitive regular expression to find.

limit.description: Maximum matches: 20 by default, 200 at most.

tools.name: CanvasWait
tools.description: Wait for any of several nodes — your children by default: the nodes you made and those you are wired to — instead of polling or sleeping. until answer (the default): one of them gives an output, an agent's answer — or a run of it ends without one, as when its model refuses, which the result says; idle: all of them are idle; exit: one of them ends; any: one of them changes at all. It answers which node it was, with the state of each; pass its next as after to the next wait, so that nothing given meanwhile is missed. No need to wait at all for an answer to come back: end your turn, and the answer wakes you as a message.

nodes.description: The nodes: their IDs (n_…) or titles. Your children when not given.

until.description: What ends the wait: answer (the default), idle, exit or any.

after.description: The next the last wait answered: outputs given since count, those before do not.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait at most, in seconds: 600 by default, 1800 at most.

tools.name: CanvasEmit
tools.description: Put something out of your node now, as its output: it goes along your edges to the nodes your output is connected to. No need to for your answer to a node's message: the answer you end that turn with goes back to it, and along your edges, by itself. What you answer the user stays with the user, unless you emit it.

title.description: A title for it, which templates read as {{title}}.

data.description: Structured data besides the text, which templates read as {{data.<path>}}.
